raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Fixes #28157.

## Motivation

The `/metrics` route mounts the Prometheus ASGI app directly. In multiprocess mode, a scrape can spend seconds collecting and rendering metrics on the request path. In the single-tokenizer prefill topology that shares a process with the bootstrap health endpoint, scrape pressure can make `/health` look dead even though the prefill process is still alive.

## Modifications

- Run the original `make_asgi_app` in a worker thread with a buffered request and response. The serving event loop no longer executes synchronous registry collection, while native OpenMetrics negotiation, gzip compression, `name[]` filtering, headers, and response bodies remain unchanged.
- Keep only one scrape in flight. Concurrent requests return `503` instead of queuing more registry work. The request is read before the occupancy check so two simultaneous callers cannot both pass the check while awaiting their request messages.
- Bound the wait with a timeout and return `504` when it expires. The background scrape remains marked in flight until it actually finishes, so repeated timeouts cannot create an unbounded pile of workers.
- Return `500` if the native app fails. Task exceptions are logged in the completion callback, including failures that happen after the caller has already received a `504`.
- Move the regression test to `test/registered/unit/utils/` and register it for CPU CI.

## Validation

The pre-rework middleware fails the native OpenMetrics regression by returning `text/plain`. The simultaneous-arrival regression was also observed failing with two `200` responses before the request read was moved ahead of the occupancy check.

On final head `50bf308c4f`:

- Six source-bound CPU tests pass with both `prometheus-client==0.26.0` and the minimum supported `0.20.0`. They execute the real helper and middleware functions from `common.py`, the unchanged committed test file, and real `make_asgi_app` instances. Coverage includes plain text, OpenMetrics, gzip, `name[]`, sequential and simultaneous scrapes, `503`, `504`, and exception logging after a timeout.
- Changed-file pre-commit passes, including Ruff, formatting, merge-conflict checks, and registered-test validation.
- `py_compile` and scoped `git diff --check` pass.

The lightweight local lane does not import the complete serving stack or run a model. Full package CI remains authoritative for that integration coverage. No GPU or serving benchmark was run; this change targets failure isolation in the metrics path.

nodes.body: The initial gate failed because the PR has no un-ci label yet. Could a maintainer add the label / trigger the standard CI when convenient? The patch only touches the /metrics exposition path and includes a narrow unit test for concurrent scrape rejection and timeout behavior.

Re-checked against current main today: `/metrics` is still mounted as the raw prometheus ASGI app, so a slow or wedged registry read runs inline and can starve the health endpoints behind the same event loop. This PR puts the scrape behind a bounded task with a timeout and returns 503 instead of hanging, with tests for the timeout and the happy path. It has been quiet for a while; if the team would rather handle this at the router/infra layer instead of in-process, I am happy to close it, just say the word.

CI note: the 12 red NPU legs from the 10-02 run are self-hosted runner failures, not test failures. Each one ends with "Executing the custom container implementation failed. Please contact your self hosted runner administrator", and the workflow's own health-check reports "PASS: no root cause failures detected". Lint and the CPU-side legs are green. Could a maintainer tag a rerun so the NPU suite gets a clean shot?

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a guarded metrics application wrapper (`_make_guarded_metrics_app`) to prevent concurrent Prometheus metrics scrapes and enforce a timeout on slow scrapes, returning 503 and 504 status codes respectively. It also adds corresponding unit tests to verify this behavior. The review feedback suggests improving exception handling by logging background task failures centrally in `clear_scrape_task` to avoid silent failures after a timeout, and simplifying the main exception block to prevent duplicate logging.

+import asyncio
+import gzip
+import logging
+import threading
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry, Counter, make_asgi_app
+
+import sglang.srt.utils.common as common_module
+from sglang.srt.utils.common import _make_guarded_metrics_app, add_prometheus_middleware
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=2, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+async def _call_asgi(app, *, headers=(), query_string=b"", receive_override=None):
+    messages = []
+
+    if receive_override is None:
+
+        async def receive():
+            return {"type": "http.request", "body": b"", "more_body": False}
+
+    else:
+        receive = receive_override
+
+    async def send(message):
+        messages.append(message)
+
+    await app(
+        {
+            "type": "http",
+            "method": "GET",
+            "path": "/metrics",
+            "headers": list(headers),
+            "query_string": query_string,
+        },
+        receive,
+        send,
+    )
+    return messages
+
+
+def _status(messages):
+    for message in messages:
+        if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+            return message["status"]
+    raise AssertionError("missing response start")
+
+
+def _body(messages):
+    return b"".join(
+        message.get("body", b"")
+        for message in messages
+        if message["type"] == "http.response.body"
+    )
+
+
+def _headers(messages):
+    for message in messages:
+        if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
+            return message["headers"]
+    raise AssertionError("missing response start")
+
+
+def _header_dict(messages):
+    return {name.lower(): value for name, value in _headers(messages)}
+
+
+def _slow_app(app, started, finish):
+    async def slow(scope, receive, send):
+        started.set()
+        await asyncio.to_thread(finish.wait, 1)
+        await app(scope, receive, send)
+
+    return slow
+
+
+def test_add_prometheus_middleware_keeps_native_content_negotiation():
+    async def run():
+        app = SimpleNamespace(routes=[])
+        with patch("prometheus_client.multiprocess.MultiProcessCollector"):
+            add_prometheus_middleware(app)
+        metrics_app = app.routes[-1].app
+
+        openmetrics = await _call_asgi(
+            metrics_app,
+            headers=[(b"accept", b"application/openmetrics-text; version=1.0.0")],
+        )
+        assert _status(openmetrics) == 200
+        assert _header_dict(openmetrics)[b"content-type"].startswith(
+            b"application/openmetrics-text"
+        )
+        assert _body(openmetrics).endswith(b"# EOF\n")
+
+        compressed = await _call_asgi(
+            metrics_app, headers=[(b"accept-encoding", b"gzip")]
+        )
+        assert _status(compressed) == 200
+        assert _header_dict(compressed)[b"content-encoding"] == b"gzip"
+        gzip.decompress(_body(compressed))
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+def test_metrics_guard_preserves_native_prometheus_protocol():
+    async def run():
+        registry = CollectorRegistry()
+        requests = Counter("requests_total", "Requests", ["route"], registry=registry)
+        requests.labels(route="/generate").inc(3)
+        Counter("other_total", "Other", registry=registry).inc()
+        native_app = make_asgi_app(registry=registry)
+        guarded_app = _make_guarded_metrics_app(native_app)
+        cases = [
+            (),
+            ((b"accept", b"application/openmetrics-text; version=1.0.0"),),
+            ((b"accept-encoding", b"gzip"),),
+            ((b"accept", b"text/plain; version=1.0.0; escaping=underscores"),),
+        ]
+
+        for headers in cases:
+            expected = await _call_asgi(native_app, headers=headers)
+            actual = await _call_asgi(guarded_app, headers=headers)
+            assert _status(actual) == _status(expected) == 200
+            assert _headers(actual) == _headers(expected)
+            expected_body = _body(expected)
+            actual_body = _body(actual)
+            if _header_dict(expected).get(b"content-encoding") == b"gzip":
+                expected_body = gzip.decompress(expected_body)
+                actual_body = gzip.decompress(actual_body)
+            assert actual_body == expected_body
+
+        expected = await _call_asgi(native_app, query_string=b"name[]=requests_total")
+        actual = await _call_asgi(guarded_app, query_string=b"name[]=requests_total")
+        assert _status(actual) == _status(expected) == 200
+        assert _headers(actual) == _headers(expected)
+        assert _body(actual) == _body(expected)
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+def test_metrics_guard_rejects_concurrent_scrape():
+    async def run():
+        started = threading.Event()
+        finish = threading.Event()
+        registry = CollectorRegistry()
+        app = _make_guarded_metrics_app(
+            _slow_app(make_asgi_app(registry=registry), started, finish),
+            scrape_timeout_s=1.0,
+        )
+        first = asyncio.create_task(_call_asgi(app))
+        assert await asyncio.to_thread(started.wait, 1)
+
+        second_messages = await _call_asgi(app)
+        finish.set()
+        first_messages = await first
+
+        assert _status(second_messages) == 503
+        assert _status(first_messages) == 200
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+def test_metrics_guard_singleflight_covers_request_read_window():
+    async def run():
+        arrivals = 0
+        invocations = 0
+        release = asyncio.Event()
+        started = threading.Event()
+        finish = threading.Event()
+
+        async def receive():
+            nonlocal arrivals
+            arrivals += 1
+            if arrivals == 2:
+                release.set()
+            await release.wait()
+            return {"type": "http.request", "body": b"", "more_body": False}
+
+        async def metrics_app(scope, receive, send):
+            nonlocal invocations
+            invocations += 1
+            started.set()
+            await asyncio.to_thread(finish.wait, 1)
+            await send({"type": "http.response.start", "status": 200, "headers": []})
+            await send({"type": "http.response.body", "body": b"ok\n"})
+
+        app = _make_guarded_metrics_app(metrics_app, scrape_timeout_s=1.0)
+        requests = [
+            asyncio.create_task(_call_asgi(app, receive_override=receive))
+            for _ in range(2)
+        ]
+        assert await asyncio.to_thread(started.wait, 1)
+        finish.set()
+        results = await asyncio.gather(*requests)
+
+        assert sorted(_status(result) for result in results) == [200, 503]
+        assert invocations == 1
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+def test_metrics_guard_times_out_slow_scrape():
+    async def run():
+        started = threading.Event()
+        finish = threading.Event()
+        registry = CollectorRegistry()
+        app = _make_guarded_metrics_app(
+            _slow_app(make_asgi_app(registry=registry), started, finish),
+            scrape_timeout_s=0.01,
+        )
+        messages = await _call_asgi(app)
+        assert started.is_set()
+        finish.set()
+
+        assert _status(messages) == 504
+        assert _body(messages) == b"metrics scrape timed out\n"
+
+    asyncio.run(run())
+
+
+def test_metrics_guard_logs_background_failure_after_timeout(caplog):
+    async def run():
+        started = threading.Event()
+        finish = threading.Event()
+        failed = threading.Event()
+
+        async def metrics_app(scope, receive, send):
+            started.set()
+            await asyncio.to_thread(finish.wait, 1)
+            failed.set()
+            raise RuntimeError("registry read failed")
+
+        app = _make_guarded_metrics_app(metrics_app, scrape_timeout_s=0.01)
+        caplog.set_level(logging.ERROR, logger=common_module.logger.name)
+        messages = await _call_asgi(app)
+        assert _status(messages) == 504
+        assert started.is_set()
+        finish.set()
+        assert await asyncio.to_thread(failed.wait, 1)
+
+        deadline = asyncio.get_running_loop().time() + 1
+        while not caplog.records and asyncio.get_running_loop().time() < deadline:
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
+
+        assert any(
+            record.message == "Failed to generate Prometheus metrics"
+            and record.exc_info is not None
+            and record.exc_info[0] is RuntimeError
+            for record in caplog.records
+        )
+
+    asyncio.run(run())

issue_comments.body: The initial gate failed because the PR has no un-ci label yet. Could a maintainer add the label / trigger the standard CI when convenient? The patch only touches the /metrics exposition path and includes a narrow unit test for concurrent scrape rejection and timeout behavior.

Re-checked against current main today: `/metrics` is still mounted as the raw prometheus ASGI app, so a slow or wedged registry read runs inline and can starve the health endpoints behind the same event loop. This PR puts the scrape behind a bounded task with a timeout and returns 503 instead of hanging, with tests for the timeout and the happy path. It has been quiet for a while; if the team would rather handle this at the router/infra layer instead of in-process, I am happy to close it, just say the word.

CI note: the 12 red NPU legs from the 10-02 run are self-hosted runner failures, not test failures. Each one ends with "Executing the custom container implementation failed. Please contact your self hosted runner administrator", and the workflow's own health-check reports "PASS: no root cause failures detected". Lint and the CPU-side legs are green. Could a maintainer tag a rerun so the NPU suite gets a clean shot?

reviews.body:
## Code Review

This pull request introduces a guarded metrics application wrapper (`_make_guarded_metrics_app`) to prevent concurrent Prometheus metrics scrapes and enforce a timeout on slow scrapes, returning 503 and 504 status codes respectively. It also adds corresponding unit tests to verify this behavior. The review feedback suggests improving exception handling by logging background task failures centrally in `clear_scrape_task` to avoid silent failures after a timeout, and simplifying the main exception block to prevent duplicate logging.
